title: AI: Research agents
summary: Two stories meet the multi-source threshold: the existing OpenAI–PerturbAI research report and BBC reporting on Google staff resignations over military AI contracts. The OpenAI–Google Cloud agreement is omitted because it appeared in the Oct. 22 edition; other collected launches and demos lacked independent follow-up coverage.

stories.headline: Using thousands of AI agents to uncover new leads in biological data
stories.dek: OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps Research described a parallel analysis of mouse-brain cell data that generated hypotheses for follow-up experiments.
tldr: OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps Research said thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents analyzed experimental data from millions of mouse brain cells in 32 minutes.
The system connected gene disruptions, cellular responses, and scientific literature to produce a reasoning atlas with candidate biological mechanisms.
The reported output is a set of research leads that still require experiments; it is not evidence that the proposed mechanisms or treatments are established.

body.text: OpenAI described a collaboration with PerturbAI and Scripps Research in which thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents analyzed existing experimental data from millions of mouse brain cells. The teams said the parallel analysis and synthesis took 32 minutes. [1][2]

The agents examined gene disruptions, cellular responses, and scientific literature, then combined their reports into a reasoning atlas linking genes, cell effects, publications, and possible mechanisms. The partner announcement describes the dataset as an 8-million-cell, whole-brain CRISPR atlas. [1][2]

The teams reported that the system reproduced findings from human analyses and surfaced additional leads, including a possible connection involving cholesterol regulation and neurodegeneration. They also said blinded human experts’ assessments of novelty and scientific value aligned with the agents’ evaluations. [1][2]

These are hypotheses drawn from existing data and literature, not demonstrated treatment effects or validated disease mechanisms. The researchers said follow-up experiments are needed to test the proposed connections, so the clinical relevance and reproducibility of the leads remain unresolved. [1][2]

stories.whyItMatters: The case shows how agent systems may help researchers search large experimental datasets and prioritize hypotheses. Its practical value depends on whether the proposed links survive experimental follow-up, which the announcement does not yet establish.
stories.editorNote: OpenAI and PerturbAI announcements agree on the workflow and 32-minute analysis. Treated findings as hypotheses pending experiments.

stories.headline: Google staff resign in backlash over its AI contracts with military
stories.dek: The BBC reported that several Google DeepMind employees resigned over military uses of the company’s AI technology.
tldr: The BBC reported that several Google DeepMind employees resigned over Google’s AI contracts with military customers.
One former employee spoke to the BBC about her concerns, while the report also placed the dispute in the context of earlier criticism of Project Nimbus.
The cited coverage does not establish the scale of the resignations or detail the terms and operational scope of the military contracts.

body.text: The BBC reported that several Google DeepMind employees had resigned amid concern about Google’s artificial intelligence contracts with military customers. The report includes an interview with one employee who said she left the company that week. [1]

The BBC said the former employee spoke despite contractual restrictions on discussing her departure. Its reporting centers on internal objections to military applications of Google’s AI systems; it does not provide a full list of resigning staff. [1]

The report also refers to Project Nimbus, the $1.2bn joint cloud and AI contract between Google and Amazon that has drawn criticism from employees since 2024. That earlier dispute is context for the current resignations, rather than evidence that the current contracts have identical terms. [1]

A Reddit discussion linked to the BBC report shows the story received public attention, but comments there are reactions rather than independent confirmation of the underlying employment claims. The number of departures, the relevant contract details, and any response from Google remain unclear in the cited material. [1][2]

stories.whyItMatters: The resignations put a workforce and governance dimension on the growing use of commercial AI systems in defense. The available reporting documents employee objections but leaves the contracts’ precise scope and the size of the departures unresolved.
stories.editorNote: BBC reporting is the factual basis; a scored Reddit discussion is included only as a separate public discussion source. It is not treated as independent confirmation of the reported departures.
